extracted.intended_audience: NRC licensees, NRC staff, nuclear plant operators, and regulatory stakeholders (parties seeking exemptions under 10 CFR part 50)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and guidance for NRC staff and licensees on evaluating and requesting exemptions under 10 CFR 50.12 to allow withdrawals from decommissioning trust funds (DTFs) for disposal of major radioactive components (MRCs) during operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions authorized by law
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 10 CFR 50.12, the Commission may grant exemptions from the requirements of 10 CFR part 50 when the exemptions are authorized by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff must determine that granting the exemption would not result in a violation of the Atomic Energy Act or the Commission's regulations. The exemption request should demonstrate that reasonable assurance of adequate funding for radiological decommissioning will continue despite the withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will not present an undue risk to the public health and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the statutory criteria for granting an exemption is that it will not present an undue risk to the public health and safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the exemption would not alter plant equipment operation, introduce new industrial/radiological/chemical hazards, or remove design or operation controls or safeguards. Show that the exemption does not diminish the effectiveness of other regulations (e.g., 10 CFR 50.82(a)(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent with the common defense and security
rubrics_metrics.description: An exemption must be consistent with the common defense and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that the exemption will not adversely affect the licensee's ability to physically secure the site or protect special nuclear material and that it has no relation to physical security issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of special circumstances under 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: An exemption will not be considered unless special circumstances are present as listed in 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(i)-(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant special circumstances include: (ii) application of the regulation in the particular circumstances would not serve or is not necessary to achieve the underlying purpose of the rule; and (iii) compliance would result in undue hardship or other costs significantly in excess of those contemplated when the regulation was adopted or incurred by others similarly situated. The request should explain which special circumstance(s) applies and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application would not serve underlying purpose of rule (10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Special circumstances exist when strict application of the regulation would not serve the underlying purpose of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the underlying purpose (e.g., ensuring reasonable assurance of funding for decommissioning within required timeframe) would still be met despite the exemption. Provide site-specific financial analyses that show the exemption does not frustrate the regulation's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance would result in undue hardship (10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Special circumstances exist when compliance would create undue hardship or costs significantly greater than contemplated by the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the undue hardship (e.g., need to construct additional storage facility with estimated construction, maintenance, and decommissioning costs) and show that using DTF funds would avoid these excessive costs. Include estimates and comparisons to costs already collected in the DTF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary-circumstances / totality-of-facts evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: DTF withdrawals for MRC disposal during operations will be granted only in 'extraordinary circumstances' and are evaluated on the totality of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive, site-specific justification, including financial status reports, cost estimates, and operational constraints. The NRC will weigh all relevant facts when deciding whether circumstances are extraordinary.

rubrics_metrics.name: DTF withdrawals permissible only if DTF contains excess funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawals from the DTF during operations to pay for offsite disposal of MRCs may be used only when the total DTF contains funds in excess of cost estimates to complete all required radiological decommissioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees may use economic projections for future years when calculating excess funds, but must account for potential economic changes that could cause future shortfalls. Provide DTF valuations and show excess beyond minimum required financial assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of decommissioning and MRCs (10 CFR 50.2) and ISG position
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation's definition of decommissioning (10 CFR 50.2) addresses removing a facility or site from service and reducing residual radioactivity and does not include activities associated with disposal of MRCs during operations. MRC means reactor vessel and internals, steam generators, pressurizers, large bore RCS piping, and other large components radioactive to a comparable degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim Staff Guidance clarifies that removal/disposal or storage of MRCs during operations is generally a business cost and not a legitimate decommissioning activity; however, after permanent cessation of operations MRC disposal is a legitimate decommissioning expense. Exemption requests must address this distinction and justify why an exception is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements in 10 CFR 50.82(a)(8)(i) and (ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: 10 CFR 50.82(a)(8)(i) restricts withdrawals to legitimate decommissioning activities; 10 CFR 50.82(a)(8)(ii) discusses timing, allowing limited planning withdrawals and restricting further withdrawals until certifications under 10 CFR 50.82(a)(1) are submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why timing restrictions should be relaxed for the requested withdrawal (e.g., capacity limits, imminent component removal) and how the requested early withdrawal is essentially an acceleration of an otherwise permissible withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NRC methodologies and supporting documents (NUREG-1307, funding status reports, cash-flow analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC staff uses the licensee's decommissioning funding status report (10 CFR 50.75), NUREG-1307 methodology, site-specific decommissioning cost estimates, and cash-flow analyses to evaluate exemption requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit decommissioning funding status reports, site-specific cost estimates, and cash-flow analyses prepared in accordance with NRC methodologies (e.g., NUREG-1307). The staff will perform independent analysis to verify that the withdrawal will not adversely impact termination ability within required timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable assurance that adequate funding remains for decommissioning
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff must determine that continued reasonable assurance of adequate funding for radiological decommissioning exists despite the proposed withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show quantitative comparisons: minimum required financial assurance versus total DTF market value (net of material tax liabilities) and demonstrate that using the requested amount (e.g., not to exceed $20 million per unit in this case) will not negatively impact ability to decommission within required timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental assessment and FONSI requirements (10 CFR 51.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC must consider whether the proposed exemption would have significant environmental impacts and prepare an environmental assessment under 10 CFR 51.30; if no significant impact is found, publish a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide environmental information necessary for the staff's EA. The final determination may result in a FONSI and no need for an EIS if impacts are not significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption-specific limits and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions can be granted with specific monetary limits and other conditions (e.g., this action allowed withdrawals not to exceed $20 million per unit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should propose clear limits/conditions and the staff may impose specific maximum amounts, effective dates, or other conditions to ensure compliance with underlying regulatory purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions must not alter safe operation or security controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting an exemption should not alter the design, function, or operation of structures/systems necessary to maintain safety/security, nor affect the licensee's ability to secure the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the exemption concerns only funding uses and will not change operational or security measures; show no new hazards or reduction in protective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between business decisions and decommissioning expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal/replacement/disposal or storage of MRCs during operations is typically a business decision and should be funded by the licensee's operating funds, whereas disposal after permanent cessation is a decommissioning expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting an exemption to fund MRC disposal from the DTF during operations, explicitly justify why this particular instance is an exception to the general business-cost rule (e.g., mausoleum capacity, imminent component removal, cost-benefit of avoiding new storage construction).
